nearest_prior_work: Clark (1987) states the classical discrete Gronwall product bound x_n <= a* product_j(1+b_j).
Yang (1988) places broader linear and nonlinear difference inequalities explicitly in the discrete Gronwall-Bellman family.
The implication that an integer-valued quantity with absolute value below one is zero is elementary lattice discreteness, not a separate recurrence theorem.
classification.attribution: Attribute the multiplicative boundedness step to the discrete Grönwall tradition, with Clark's product form as the nearest exact source. Credit the local Lean asset for combining that bound with normalized vanishing of an integral signed defect and for the exact reciprocal-tail Sylvester consumer.
classification.mathematical_interest: The theorem is not deep as an inequality, but it is a clean termination interface: all analytic work is isolated in summability and normalized vanishing, after which discreteness forces exactness.
classification.reusable_scope: Positive integer-valued heights satisfying C_{n+1} <= C_n(1+delta_n), with summable nonnegative delta_n and an integer defect negligible relative to C_n.
classification.why_it_matters: It converts asymptotic smallness into eventual exact recurrence and makes clear that proving delta_n -> 0 is insufficient; total one-sided relative growth must be summable for this route.

primary_sources.title: Short proof of a discrete Gronwall inequality
primary_sources.author: Dean S. Clark
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Abstract and main inequality: x_n <= a* product_{j=n0}^{n-1}(1+b_j) under a standard discrete Gronwall recurrence.
primary_sources.supports: The product-growth bound used to show that summable relative growth keeps C_n bounded.
primary_sources.does_not_support: No integer-defect extinction statement, normalized-vanishing hypothesis, reciprocal-tail orbit, or Sylvester consequence.

primary_sources.title: On some new discrete generalizations of Gronwall's inequality
primary_sources.author: En Hao Yang
primary_sources.venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 129 (1988), 505-516
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Abstract and Theorem 3: general linear Bellman-type discrete inequalities in one independent variable.
primary_sources.supports: Established difference-inequality terminology and the broader recurrence setting for discrete Grönwall bounds.
primary_sources.does_not_support: No signed negative-mass normalization or eventual integral extinction.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: From C_{n+1} <= C_n(1+delta_n), iteration gives C_n <= C_0 product_{i<n}(1+delta_i); summability of delta bounds this product.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The exact update identifies delta_n with only the negative part of an integer defect, and the normalized-vanishing hypothesis is strong enough to turn bounded C_n into eventual |E_n|<1.
mechanism_comparison.bounded_tail_endpoint: Once C_n is uniformly bounded, the named Lean consumer chooses a normalization parameter above that bound and uses integer-lattice discreteness directly. The summable negative-mass theorem supplies boundedness through the classical product estimate, so this endpoint is a proof layer rather than a separate theorem class.
mechanism_comparison.sharpness_boundary: Replacing sum delta_n < infinity by delta_n -> 0 breaks the argument and the conclusion: C_n=n+1, E_n=-1 has harmonic relative mass and never terminates.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The abstract lemma is reusable and worth retaining, but its significance is as a producer-consumer interface rather than as an independently novel inequality.
